assumptions: Capture reagents with validated buffer compatibility are available or can be developed.
Sufficient conditioned-medium yield exists to run matrixed device/formulation compatibility testing across >=3 independent lots.
In vitro membrane-protected bioactivity assay can be established and reasonably scaled for matrix testing.
biological_rationale: Large-animal intranasal biodistribution and MISEV2023 consensus indicate that particle counts and rodent intranasal localization are insufficient to infer preserved intact-EV identity or functional cargo after formulation and device exposure. A spike-in-controlled orthogonal workflow protects against assay failure and distinguishes true loss of membrane-protected signatures from capture-reagent or buffer interference.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail: spike-in recovery in capture-positive particle-peak fractions that is lost after detergent+protease (validated) and endogenous capture co-localization preserved.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Spike-in-validated orthogonal identity preservation after device/formulation passage
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Controls for assay recovery and discriminates true loss of membrane-protected EV signatures from reagent/buffer interference; required before treating material as EV-enriched for bridging studies.

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative presence/absence of detergent/protease-sensitive reduction in LPS-induced cytokine release in capture-positive fraction eluates (yes/no across >=3 lots).
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Preserved membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity in capture-positive fractions after device/formulation passage
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: Functional confirmation that preserved identity corresponds to membrane-protected activity; supports potency linkage without premature numeric specification.

edges.competing_explanation: Observed loss of capture signal could reflect capture-reagent/formulation incompatibility rather than true membrane/cargo loss.
edges.missing_experiment: Paired capture-compatibility controls for each formulation/device exposure and inclusion of exogenous spike-in tracer to rule out assay interference.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal controls; program-specific device/formulation effects need empirical validation.

edges.competing_explanation: Large-animal lack of detectable EV signal may be due to administration route or species clearance rather than device/formulation-induced masking.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recovery tests with spike-in-controlled orthogonal capture to link in vitro compatibility with in vivo detectability.
edges.uncertainty: High: large-animal negative biodistribution increases importance of validating identity preservation before bridging, but species-specific clearance may still limit detectability.

nodes.statement: Device passage or formulation excipients can mask epitopes or disrupt EV membranes, abolishing capture-positive surface-phenotype while leaving bulk particle counts similar.

Recovery of an exogenous intact-EV spike-in in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions with detergent/protease sensitivity validates assay performance and discriminates true identity loss from assay interference.

Preservation of spike-in-validated orthogonal identity plus membrane-protected in vitro bioactivity after device/formulation passage indicates compatibility suitable to gate an EV-enriched drug-substance for further CMC and bridging work.

competing_explanations: Apparent preserved spike-in recovery could mask loss of endogenous EVs if spike-in behaves differently; simultaneous endogenous readouts are necessary.
design_question: How should formulation and device compatibility be tested without assuming preserved EV identity or activity?
expected_measurable_effect: Identification of at least one formulation/device condition that preserves (A) spike-in-protected recovery in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions with detergent/protease sensitivity and (B) a membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity in captured fractions across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots (qualitative pass).

experiment.assay: Parallel orthogonal workflows: spike-in addition prior to device/formulation passage; device passage simulation; fractionation to identify particle peaks; immuno-capture readouts distinguishing spike-in and endogenous signals; detergent+protease protection; in vitro bioassay on captured eluates.
experiment.comparator: No-exposure control (baseline buffer, no device passage) versus matrixed formulation/device conditions; include detergent+protease-disrupted aliquots and capture-compatibility controls.
experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EV prep and dexamethasone in bioassay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer-only fractions. Capture-compatibility and spike-in controls for each buffer/device.
dependencies: Access to validated spike-in tracer and capture reagents with buffer-compatibility data
Sufficient conditioned-medium yield for >=3 independent lots
Analytical capacity for orthogonal assays and in vitro bioassay
experiment.failure_criterion: After capture-compatibility controls, no tested condition reproducibly preserves both identity and protected bioactivity across >=3 lots, or all observed preservations are explained by assay interference.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, do not adopt EV-enriched compatibility gate for intranasal route; consider secretome-centric strategies, immediate capture/lyophilization, alternative delivery routes, or reformulation/reagent redesign.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: Specific formulation excipient classes and delivery-device shear exposures will either preserve or abolish an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (spike-in-validated capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks + detergent/protease sensitivity) and a matched membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative preservation (yes/no) per condition of (A) spike-in recovery in capture-positive particle-peak fractions that is lost after detergent+protease and (B) presence of membrane-protected anti-inflammatory effect in captured eluates that is abolished after detergent+protease; reproducible across >=3 lots.
experiment.question: Which nasal excipient classes and device-shear exposures preserve the orthogonal intact-EV identity signature and membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory bioactivity versus those that abolish both, independent of bulk particle counts?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed to yield an enriched small-EV fraction sufficient for matrixing
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (non-overlapping species or isotope-labeled)
Panel of candidate formulation buffers/excipient classes (matrix across pH, ionic strength, non-ionic surfactant levels, chelators, sugars/polyols)
Device-shear simulation rigs or representative nasal spray devices with characterized shear/pressure profiles
Immuno-capture reagents for canonical EV surface markers and capture-compatibility control panels
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100) for membrane disruption controls
Density-fractionation materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Standardized in vitro neuroinflammation assay platform (LPS-stimulated microglia IL-6/TNF-α readout)
secondary_readouts: Mass and particle recovery after formulation/device exposure
experiment.success_criterion: For >=1 formulation/device condition representative of intended clinical use, across >=3 independent lots the condition reproducibly preserves both (A) spike-in-validated orthogonal identity and (B) membrane-protected in vitro bioactivity while capture-compatibility controls exclude assay interference.

explicit_inferences: Spike-in controls are required to separate assay failure from true loss of EV-associated signatures.
Preservation of orthogonal identity metrics after device/formulation passage is necessary (but not sufficient) evidence to advance lots into bridging studies.
falsification_criteria: Validated spike-in recovery observed but endogenous capture-positive co-localization and membrane-protected bioactivity are not reproducibly observed in bounded fractions across >=3 lots (falsifies EV-enriched compatibility gate).
Capture-compatibility controls indicate observed capture-signal loss is attributable entirely to assay interference, preventing discrimination; reformulation or reagent change required.
human_decisions_required: Select spike-in tracer and validate its behavior relative to endogenous EVs.
Define the set of formulation excipient classes and representative device shear profiles to test.
Decide pass/fail qualitative rules for the compatibility gate and regulatory briefing approach.
manufacturability_assessment: Feasible as a qualitative gate. Requires development of an exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and analytical harmonization for capture/protection assays. Device and formulation simulation rigs may be needed. Resource and timeline moderate (assay development and matrixed testing across lots).
manufacturing_rationale: Defining a qualitative compatibility gate (non-numeric) that requires assay-validated preservation of orthogonal identity and protected bioactivity will de-risk downstream GMP-like scale-up, comparability, and regulator engagement by ensuring lots advanced for bridging studies have a reproducible drug-substance identity that survived formulation and device passage.
measurement_strategy: Matrixed orthogonal workflow: spike-in addition prior to device/formulation exposure; passage through device or simulation rig; fractionation (SEC or iodixanol cushion) to identify particle peaks; immuno-capture readouts for multiple epitopes distinguishing endogenous and spike-in signals; detergent+protease protection assays; targeted in vitro neuroinflammation assay on captured eluates; capture-compatibility controls per buffer and device rinse.
novelty_statement: When capture-compatibility conflicts exist, this proposal changes the substantive discriminating experiment by adding an exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and requiring preserved membrane-protected in vitro bioactivity after device/formulation passage (not just surface-marker readout). This materially distinguishes true identity preservation from assay interference and provides a discriminating in vitro functional correlate to the identity metric.
principal_risks: Assay interference producing false negatives (capture-reagent incompatibility with formulation buffers).
Spike-in behavior differing from endogenous EVs, limiting interpretability if endogenous signals are weak.
In vivo delivery barriers (species, administration route) may still prevent brain exposure despite preserved in vitro signatures.
proposed_potency_relationship: If preserved identity (spike-in-validated capture co-localization and detergent/protease sensitivity) co-occurs with preserved membrane-protected in vitro bioactivity across lots, treat the composite outcome as a qualitative potency-linked gate for advancing lots into bridging studies.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a non-assumptive compatibility gate: require preservation of an orthogonal intact-EV identity signature (spike-in-protected recovery + multi-epitope capture co-localizing with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) together with preserved membrane-protected in vitro bioactivity in capture-positive fractions after device/formulation passage before treating a material as an EV-enriched drug-substance for intranasal use.
title: Intranasal formulation compatibility — spike-in-controlled orthogonal identity and compatibility test
